home.hero.subtitle: Mīzān is an evidence-based Hanafi system for Zakah and Islamic inheritance. Every result is explained with its ruling, conditions and sources — and unsupported cases are refused rather than guessed.
home.principle.noFabrication.title: No fabricated rulings
home.principle.noFabrication.body: Rules are researcher-maintained and carry an explicit verification status. Unverified scenarios are refused, not guessed.
home.principle.exactArithmetic.title: Exact arithmetic
home.principle.exactArithmetic.body: Inheritance fractions use BigInt rationals. No floating-point drift in the share mathematics; rounding only at the final amount.
home.principle.explained.title: Explained, not just calculated
home.principle.explained.body: Every step exposes its calculation, fiqh principle, reason, evidence tooltip and rule identifier.

about.project.title: About the Project
about.project.p1: This project, titled “Design and Development of an Islamic Zakah and Inheritance Calculation System Based on Established Fiqh Principles,” aims to develop an accessible and evidence-based digital platform for calculating Islamic Zakah and distributing inheritance according to established Hanafi jurisprudential principles.
about.project.p2: The system is designed not only to provide accurate calculations but also to explain the underlying Islamic legal principles, relevant conditions, supporting evidences, and scholarly references behind each result.
about.project.p3: Through the integration of Islamic jurisprudential knowledge and modern web technologies, this research seeks to make the understanding and practical application of Zakah and Islamic inheritance more accessible, transparent, and systematic.
about.project.p4: The initial implementation follows the Hanafi Madhhab, with an extensible architecture designed to accommodate other recognized schools of Islamic jurisprudence in future development.
about.academicNote: This application is an independent academic project. It does not claim official endorsement by the International Islamic University Chittagong or any other institution.
methodology.title: Academic Methodology
methodology.description: How jurisprudential rules become deterministic, explainable software — and where the limits are.
methodology.card.versioned.title: Versioned rules
methodology.card.versioned.body: Every calculation records `hanafi-v1.0.0` and its engine version. A future rule change creates a new version instead of rewriting history.
methodology.card.fractions.title: Exact fractions
methodology.card.fractions.body: Inheritance shares use BigInt rational numbers. Currency rounding happens only when an amount is presented or saved.
methodology.card.scope.title: Conservative scope
methodology.card.scope.body: Only high-confidence rules are encoded. Ambiguous combinations return a verification message instead of a possibly incorrect distribution.
methodology.verification.title: Verification statuses
methodology.verification.description: Every evidence item and rule exposes one of these states.
methodology.verification.VERIFIED_BY_SCH: Reviewed and confirmed by a qualified scholar for this methodology version.
methodology.verification.REFERENCE_REQUI: The rule is implemented, but the exact bibliographic reference still needs verification.
methodology.verification.NEEDS_REVIEW: The application records a position, but a scholar must confirm its application to modern cases.
methodology.verification.UNVERIFIED: No reliable position is encoded; the scenario is refused by the engine.
methodology.pipeline.title: Calculation pipeline
methodology.pipeline.description: Separation of presentation, jurisprudence, calculation and persistence.
methodology.pipeline.stage1.title: 1 · Presentation layer
methodology.pipeline.stage1.body: React forms collect inputs. The UI never calculates a jurisprudential decision on its own.
methodology.pipeline.stage2.title: 2 · Validation layer
methodology.pipeline.stage2.body: Zod schemas validate every request on the server before the engine is called.
methodology.pipeline.stage3.title: 3 · Fiqh rule registry
methodology.pipeline.stage3.body: Versioned rule objects carry a rule ID, principle, evidence and verification status.
methodology.pipeline.stage4.title: 4 · Calculation engine
methodology.pipeline.stage4.body: Pure deterministic functions produce shares, classifications and structured explanation steps.
methodology.pipeline.stage5.title: 5 · Persistence layer
methodology.pipeline.stage5.body: Prisma stores the input snapshot and the methodology version used, so old results never change silently.
methodology.unsupported.title: Unsupported scenarios
methodology.unsupported.body: When a case is not backed by a verified rule, the engine returns the following message rather than a potentially incorrect distribution:
methodology.unsupported.limitations: Current deliberate limitations include the grandfather-with-siblings combination, distant kindred, uncles and nephews, and modern assets without a verified Zakah policy. These are documented TODOs for scholarly review, not silent omissions.

nisab.explainer.what.title: What is Nisab?
nisab.explainer.what.body: Nisab (النصاب) is the minimum threshold of wealth at which Zakah becomes obligatory. Below it, no Zakah is due; at or above it, the applicable rate is applied once the other conditions are met.
nisab.explainer.why.title: Why is it important?
nisab.explainer.why.body: It separates wealth that is sufficient for Zakah from wealth that is not. The threshold is a condition of obligation, not a deduction from the wealth.
nisab.explainer.gold.title: Classical gold weight
nisab.explainer.gold.body: The classical threshold is 20 mithqal of gold. The gram equivalent used here is 85 g, stored as a configurable weight. The exact conversion depends on the mithqal standard adopted and must be verified against a cited source.
nisab.explainer.silver.title: Classical silver weight
nisab.explainer.silver.body: The classical threshold is 200 dirhams of silver. The gram equivalent used here is 595 g, stored as a configurable weight. As with gold, the conversion and its source require verification.
nisab.explainer.differ.title: Why the monetary values differ
nisab.explainer.differ.body: Gold and silver have independent market prices. The same classical weights therefore produce two different monetary thresholds. Many contemporary scholars prefer the silver threshold because it is lower and includes more people; this is a methodological choice, not a universal consensus.
nisab.explainer.which.title: Which threshold is applied?
nisab.explainer.which.body: The calculator lets you select the gold or silver method and displays the method used in every result. The default is silver, and the rationale is recorded in the seeded Nisab configuration.
